_readme: Add a series by adding an entry here — no new script needed.
Run one source:  MODE=discover python scripts/fetch.py NAME   (dump real structure first)
Providers: fred (any FRED id) | eurostat (any dataset+params) | owid (any grapher slug) | csv (any URL)
Everything runs in GitHub Actions — the dev sandbox cannot reach these hosts.

sources.name: cattle-herd
sources.source: FAOSTAT cattle stocks (head), via Our World in Data

sources.name: us-prices
sources.source: BLS producer price indexes via FRED, plus CPI for deflating
sources.note: PPI levels are index numbers (1982=100) — ratios only, never quantities

sources.name: eu-vet-expenses
sources.source: Eurostat Economic Accounts for Agriculture, veterinary expenses
sources.note: ALL livestock, not cattle only — do not present as a per-cattle figure without saying so

sources.name: eu-hicp
sources.source: Euro area HICP via FRED — deflator for any EUR money series

sources.name: vetapi-probe
sources.source: Discovery only — FRED series headers plus a candidate-id probe
sources.note: MODE=discover only. A guessed FRED id returns an HTML error page, not an error — probe before parsing, and read the Title off FRED rather than inferring it from the id. The BLS catalogue files return 403 to this fetcher.

sources.name: vetapi-us
sources.source: BLS producer price indexes via FRED, titles read off FRED not inferred from the id: PCU325411325411 'PPI by Industry: Medicinal and Botanical Manufacturing' (index Jun 1982=100, monthly, 1982-06→) = the bulk active-ingredient stage; PCU325412325412 'PPI by Industry: Pharmaceutical Preparation Manufacturing' (index Jun 1981=100, monthly, 1981-06→) = the finished dose; WPU063808 'PPI by Commodity: Pharmaceuticals Affecting Parasitic and Infective Diseases' (index Jun 2001=100, monthly, 2001-06→); PCU325414325414 'PPI by Industry: Other Biological Product Manufacturing' (index Jun 1991=100, monthly, 1991-06→) = vaccines and biologicals; CPIAUCSL to deflate
sources.note: THE TWO SPINE SERIES SIT ON DIFFERENT BASE MONTHS — Jun 1982 and Jun 1981. Their raw ratio therefore has no interpretable level at all; only its change between two dates means anything. BLS publishes NO veterinary-only price index: every product line that could be checked is labelled 'for Human Use'. WPU063808 (antiparasitics and anti-infectives) and PCU325414325414 (biologicals/vaccines) are the closest therapeutic proxies to a livestock portfolio, and they still cover human products too.

sources.name: vetapi-eu
sources.source: Eurostat sts_inpp_a, industrial domestic producer price index, geo EU27_2020, unit I15 (index, 2015=100), annual; NACE C211 (manufacture of basic pharmaceutical products), C212 (manufacture of pharmaceutical preparations), C21 (both)
sources.note: Codes confirmed against the source's own category list, not guessed. C211 is the active-ingredient stage, C212 the finished dose. The unit is pinned to I15 because the dataset also carries 2021=100 and 2010=100 — mixing them would silently blend three different bases. Covers human and veterinary pharma together; Eurostat publishes no veterinary-only split.

sources.name: vetapi-tr
sources.source: TÜİK via TCMB EVDS: TP.TUFE1YI.T59 (Yİ-ÜFE, NACE 21 temel eczacılık ürünleri ve müstahzarları), TP.TUFE1YI.T60 (Yİ-ÜFE, NACE 21.2 eczacılık müstahzarları), TP.UFEYD16 (Yurt Dışı ÜFE, NACE 21 — imported pharma input prices)
sources.note: TÜİK publishes NO standalone NACE 21.1 index. For TR the ingredient side is proxied by the imported-goods price index for NACE 21 — an import price, not a domestic ingredient price. That limitation travels with every TR number.

sources.name: us-cowcalf-costs
sources.source: USDA ERS commodity costs and returns, cow-calf
sources.note: SURVEY BASIS CHANGED IN 2008 — do not compare across that break
